summary:
**ORBITAL COMMAND – Design. Explore. Launch.**

ORBITAL COMMAND is an interactive space mission design game developed to make spacecraft engineering and mission planning easier to understand through hands-on learning.

Players take on the role of mission designers, choosing destinations such as the Moon, Mars and Deep Space. They must build a spacecraft by selecting power systems, communications equipment, propulsion, flight computers and scientific instruments. Every decision involves trade-offs between budget, spacecraft mass, power requirements, reliability and scientific value. Players then select a suitable launch vehicle and run a simulated mission, facing mission events and receiving a final performance score.

The project addresses the challenge by turning complex space mission planning concepts into an accessible and engaging interactive experience. It encourages experimentation, problem-solving and an understanding of how different spacecraft systems work together.

ORBITAL COMMAND aims to inspire curiosity about space exploration and help players appreciate the engineering decisions behind real space missions.
details:
ORBITAL COMMAND – Design. Explore. Launch.

What does the project do and how does it work?

ORBITAL COMMAND is an interactive browser-based space mission design game that allows players to experience the challenges of planning a space exploration mission.

Players begin by selecting one of three destinations: the Moon, Mars or Deep Space. They then design their spacecraft by choosing essential systems, including power generation, communications, propulsion and flight computers. They can also select scientific instruments to determine the type of information their mission will collect.

The game introduces realistic engineering trade-offs. Players must manage a limited budget, spacecraft mass, power generation and consumption, scientific value and equipment reliability. Once their spacecraft is designed, they select a suitable launch vehicle based on payload capacity, destination compatibility and available funds.

The mission is then simulated through a series of events. Players receive a final performance score based on their spacecraft design, resource management and mission outcomes.

What are the benefits?

The main benefit of ORBITAL COMMAND is that it makes complex space engineering concepts easier to understand through interactive learning.

Instead of simply reading about spacecraft, players actively make engineering decisions and see the consequences of their choices. They learn that successful space missions require different systems to work together and that improving one aspect of a spacecraft can create challenges elsewhere.

The game encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, experimentation and an interest in science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM).

What is the intended impact?

Our aim is to make space exploration more accessible and engaging, particularly for students and young people who are interested in science and technology.

We want players to develop a better understanding of the engineering and planning involved in real space missions. By allowing them to experiment with different spacecraft designs, the game encourages curiosity about space exploration and the technology used to explore our Solar System.

What tools and technologies were used?

The project was developed using standard web technologies:

  • HTML: Used to create the structure and different screens of the game.
  • CSS: Used to design the interface, spacecraft selection cards, colours, layouts and visual elements.
  • JavaScript: Used to develop the game logic, resource calculations, spacecraft selection, launch compatibility checks, mission simulation and scoring system.
  • Google Chrome: Used to run and test the game.
  • GitHub: Used to store and publish the project source code.

The game is designed to run directly in a web browser without requiring users to install additional software.

How is the project creative?

ORBITAL COMMAND combines the idea of a space exploration game with the decision-making process used in spacecraft engineering.
